title: APC UPS Output Load Percent Approaching Nameplate Limit
exclusions: Bench-grade Smart-UPS units used for workstation labs, warehouse staging racks without production VLAN dependencies, and any NMC whose SNMP agent is deprecated but still enrolled should be tagged out of alerts.
evidence: Export the saved search results showing `avg_load`, `peak_load`, `host`, and `_time` for the escalation window plus an APC NMC screenshot of output load percent that matches the polled OID reading.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=power` sourcetype='snmp:apc:ups' where `_time` satisfies `avg_load` > 80 for UC-15.1.28 ('APC UPS Output Load Percent Approaching Nameplate Limit'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `power` / `snmp:apc:ups` events where `_time` stays below `avg_load` > 80, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-15.1.28.

dataSources: APC Smart-UPS and Symmetra-class NMCs publish PowerNet-MIB `upsAdvOutputLoad` as a percentage of rated output; ingest with Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266) or the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) so events normalize to `sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups` with a parsed numeric `upsAdvOutputLoad` column suitable for host-level trending and alerting. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266), SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=power sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups host=*
| eval load_pct=tonumber(upsAdvOutputLoad)
| bin _time span=30m
| stats avg(load_pct) as avg_load, max(load_pct) as peak_load by _time, host
| where avg_load > 80 OR peak_load > 90
description: We trend APC Network Management Card telemetry for PowerNet-MIB `upsAdvOutputLoad`, the percent of nameplate capacity actually carried on the inverter output bus. Rising 30-minute averages show when a UPS is thermally and electrically closer to overload, shortening battery runtime during transfer and increasing the odds a distribution breaker opens under a surprise load step. Tracking this metric gives operations a lead time to redistribute rack power, stage a second feed, or defer installs before vendor native alarms fire during maintenance or generator tests.
value: We trend APC Network Management Card telemetry for PowerNet-MIB `upsAdvOutputLoad`, the percent of nameplat.... Timely UC-15.1.28 alerting on 'APC UPS Output Load Percent Approaching Nameplate Limit' reduces operational risk and delayed incident response before manual triage or audit channels escalate.
implementation: Poll every 1–5 minutes via Splunk Connect for SNMP (6266) or SNMP Modular Input (1537); reconcile translator outputs so high-precision APC models contribute either `upsAdvOutputLoad` or `upsHighPrecOutputLoadPercent` through a single normalized field before thresholds run. Maintain `ups_rated_kva.csv` keyed by `host` only when finance requires kW estimates from SNMP percentages. Alert when sustained `avg_load > 80` for two successive 30-minute buckets or instantaneous `peak_load > 90`, and throttle duplicates per host for at least one poll interval.
visualization: Line chart of `avg_load` by host over selectable windows, radial or gauge panel for latest `peak_load`, and horizontal bar ranking UPS hosts closest to policy limits.

references.title: Splunk Documentation: SNMP data collection overview

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `power`** — Planned work for 'APC UPS Output Load Percent Approaching Nameplate Limit' shifts `avg` over `span=30m` while `_time` remains in-scope for UC-15.1.28. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `avg` on `snmp:apc:ups`** — Scheduled automation elevates `host` without crossing `avg_load` > 80. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `_time`** — Health checks in `power` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `snmp:apc:ups`** — First 48h baseline for `_time` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `_time`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Install Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase app 6266) on a Docker host or heavy forwarder, or alternatively the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase app 1537), and pin device targets to each APC Network Management Card IP with read-only community strings stored outside configs. Confirm payloads land in `index=power` (or your operational index) as `sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups`, carrying integer `upsAdvOutputLoad` decoded from OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.318.1.1.1.4.2.3; validate against the NMC web UI `/Forms/login2` measured load pane before trusting thresholds. Configure polling every 1–5 minutes so `span=30m` aggregates in dashboards reflect at least six samples; align scheduled alert `dispatch.earliest_time` to `-15m` when polls run every five minutes to avoid blank buckets. Merge translator tweaks in `props.conf` only after comparing Symmetra models that expose `upsHighPrecOutputLoadPercent` versus legacy `upsAdvOutputLoad`. Restrict KV lookups that map rack IDs via RBAC role `power_ops_admin` for edits and `snmp_inventory_read` for analysts. Optional: mirror nightly peaks into a summary index using `collect` with `marker=summarize=true` for capacity-planning boards. Document correlation with PDU UC-15.1.7 when attributing load to specific outlets, and suppress during maintenance using a small lookup of `host` plus `window_start`/`window_end` parsed with `strptime`.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase #6266), SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase #1537) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=snmp:apc:ups into power. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, avg_load, host, peak_load`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
